en.text:
Today’s M&A briefing — 16 deals, the strategies behind them · 21 November 2026

🔹 Bending Spoons (milanese editor specializing) acquires Mailchimp (email marketing and automation platform) — $3.68bn.
Mailchimp was owned by Intuit, an American financial software group (TurboTax, QuickBooks), which bet on synergies between accounting and marketing. The operation marks the failure of this integration.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Bending Spoons does not build products from scratch: it buys installed bases, reduces costs, and monetizes more intensely — Mailchimp, with its millions of captive SMEs, is exactly the type of usage annuity this logic seeks.

🔹 Postbank (banking institution operating) acquires Fibank (banking institution operating) — €1bn.
The merger creates a significantly strengthened player in a still fragmented Bulgarian banking sector.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Banking consolidation in Central and Eastern Europe is accelerating under pressure from return on equity and increasing regulatory requirements.

🔹 Verlinvest (belgian investment fund specializing) launches a tender offer for coentreprise partagée avec Oatly — $80m.
The offer is launched at a price below the market rate, in a context where Oatly is struggling to find a convincing trajectory.

🔹 Enel (italian energy group active in renewable energy) acquires energyRe's solar project portfolio in South Carolina.

🔹 Tekever (portuguese technology group active) acquires Cloudsweep (portuguese startup specializing).

🔹 Underdogs Group acquires MotorK asset (asset from a digital marketing platform).

🔹 GSA acquires Demontes.
GSA acquires 100% of Demontes to expand its presence in Spain.

🔹 Agn Energia (gas distribution operator in Italy) acquires Turbo Gas LPG branch (liquefied petroleum gas distribution in Italy).

🔹 Tresco acquires Green Maritime (maritime transport player in the Netherlands).

🔹 Lifco (swedish conglomerate specializing) acquires Colortec (spanish manufacturer of plastic colorants).

🔹 Comfort acquires RC Drivmedelsanläggningar (fuel facilities in Sweden).

🔹 Provectus (croatian group active in healthcare services) takes a majority stake in Haelan Medical Group (medical services operator in Bulgaria).

🔹 FUNDAMENTALco acquires move38 (amsterdam-based artificial intelligence studio).

🔹 Bechtle (german IT distribution and services group) acquires HET IT (dutch IT hardware supplier).

🔹 INI acquires Grupo Azkoyen (spanish industrial group).

🔹 Global Ardour acquires Bedfordshire metal recycler (metal recycling, Bedfordshire, United Kingdom).

en.text:
Today’s fundraising briefing — 6 deals, the strategies behind them · 21 November 2026

🔹 Isomorphic Labs (design of therapeutic molecules using artificial intelligence, relying on DeepMind's AlphaFold for protein structure prediction) — $5bn · Series C.
𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀: R&D and partnerships with major pharmaceutical laboratories for the discovery phase.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: At this scale, the fundraising finances the industrial phase of AI-pharma convergence, where major laboratories seek to outsource molecule discovery.

🔹 Fractile (design of artificial intelligence chips, United Kingdom, with no commercial product at this stage) — £500m.
Fractile has no commercial product. The fundraising is part of the British strategy for technological sovereignty in semiconductors.
𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀: Machines, recruitment of engineers and computing time — almost all funds in design infrastructure.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: The presence of a sovereign fund reveals that this round finances the ability to design chips on British soil, not a product with established demand — an option purchase on technological independence.

🔹 Saviu Ventures (venture capital in Francophone Africa, French management company) — €40m.
The second fund reaches four times the size of the first. Francophone Africa remains an area poorly covered by European institutional venture capital.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Quadrupling the size of a fund between two vintages implies that the first produced convincing results and gives Saviu a quasi-monopoly position in certain Francophone African markets.

🔹 Disseqt AI (tools for testing and supervising artificial intelligence agents deployed in large companies, Dublin) — $8m.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: Rahul Dravid, former captain of the Indian national cricket team.

🔹 Stryx AI (drone detection and neutralization, early-stage French startup) — €7.7m.
Stryx AI is founded by Armand Thiberge, founder of Brevo (formerly Sendinblue), a French SaaS editor specializing in B2B marketing.

🔹 Ranketta (tools for monitoring product visibility in conversational search engine responses, ChatGPT and equivalents, Czech Republic) — €1m.
Ranketta simultaneously acquires Phemly.

fr.text:
Levées de fonds : les 6 opérations chiffrées de l'édito du 21 novembre 2026.

🔹 Isomorphic Labs (𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑝𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑚𝑜𝑙𝑒́𝑐𝑢𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑡ℎ𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑝𝑒𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠 𝑝𝑎𝑟 𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑖𝑔𝑒𝑛𝑐𝑒 𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑖𝑓𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒) — 5 Md$ · Série C.
𝗢𝗯𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗳 : R&D et partenariats avec les grands laboratoires pharmaceutiques pour la phase de découverte.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : À cette échelle, la levée finance la phase industrielle de la convergence IA-pharma, où les grands laboratoires cherchent à externaliser la découverte de molécules.

🔹 Fractile (𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑝𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑢𝑐𝑒𝑠 𝑑'𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑖𝑔𝑒𝑛𝑐𝑒 𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑖𝑓𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒, 𝑅𝑜𝑦𝑎𝑢𝑚𝑒-𝑈𝑛𝑖) — 500 M£.
Fractile n'a aucun produit commercialisé. La levée s'inscrit dans la stratégie britannique de souveraineté technologique dans les semi-conducteurs.
𝗢𝗯𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗳 : Machines, recrutement d'ingénieurs et temps de calcul — quasi-totalité des fonds en infrastructure de conception.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : La présence d'un fonds souverain révèle que ce tour finance la capacité de concevoir des puces sur le sol britannique, pas un produit dont la demande est établie — un achat d'option sur l'indépendance technologique.

🔹 Saviu Ventures (𝑐𝑎𝑝𝑖𝑡𝑎𝑙-𝑟𝑖𝑠𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑒𝑛 𝐴𝑓𝑟𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑓𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑜𝑝ℎ𝑜𝑛𝑒, 𝑠𝑜𝑐𝑖𝑒́𝑡𝑒́ 𝑑𝑒 𝑔𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑓𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑐̧𝑎𝑖𝑠𝑒) — 40 M€.
Le deuxième fonds atteint quatre fois la taille du premier. L'Afrique francophone reste un terrain peu couvert par le venture institutionnel européen.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Quadrupler la taille d'un fonds entre deux millésimes suppose que le premier a produit des résultats convaincants et confère à Saviu une position de quasi-monopole sur certains marchés d'Afrique francophone.

🔹 Disseqt AI (𝑜𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑙𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑡𝑒𝑠𝑡 𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑠𝑢𝑝𝑒𝑟𝑣𝑖𝑠𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒𝑠 𝑎𝑔𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑠 𝑑'𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑖𝑔𝑒𝑛𝑐𝑒 𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑖𝑓𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒 𝑑𝑒́𝑝𝑙𝑜𝑦𝑒́𝑠) — 8 M$.
𝗔𝘃𝗲𝗰 : Rahul Dravid, ancien capitaine de l'équipe nationale indienne de cricket.

🔹 Stryx AI (𝑑𝑒́𝑡𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑛𝑒𝑢𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑠𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑑𝑟𝑜𝑛𝑒𝑠, 𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑟𝑡-𝑢𝑝 𝑓𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑐̧𝑎𝑖𝑠𝑒 𝑎̀ 𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑟𝑒́𝑐𝑜𝑐𝑒) — 7,7 M€.
Stryx AI est fondée par Armand Thiberge, fondateur de Brevo (ex-Sendinblue), éditeur SaaS français spécialisé dans le marketing B2B.

🔹 Ranketta (𝑜𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑙𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑠𝑢𝑖𝑣𝑖 𝑑𝑒 𝑙𝑎 𝑣𝑖𝑠𝑖𝑏𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑡𝑒́ 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑𝑢𝑖𝑡𝑠) — 1 M€.
Ranketta acquiert simultanément Phemly.
